name: [Portal] Strip the admin header down to the Partner Portal shell (UI)
description:
### Summary

The design gives the Partner Portal a blue top bar containing exactly two things: a „Shoptet Partner Portal" logo on the left and the user dropdown — name, project ID, chevron — on the right (Figma `Top Bar` 542:10802, whose only children are `Left side / Logo` and `Right side / User Dropdown`). Today's admin header carries a great deal more: the Shoptet logo, a search form, and a navigation strip with search, Shoptet University, notifications, helpdesk, help, the design/dark-mode toggle, the user menu, the markets switcher and the superadmin menu. This task reduces the header to the two elements from the design on Partner Portal pages and swaps the logo for the Partner Portal wordmark. It is presentation only — no route, controller or permission changes — and the sidebar belongs to the sibling migration subtask.

### Why?

The parent task described this as „build a new React layout component", which is not where the header lives. `PageLayoutDefault` composes `NavigationMenu` (which `return null`s — it is a DOM behaviour hook, not a menu), `PageHeader` (breadcrumbs plus system messages) and `CsrfExpirationModal`. None of them renders the blue bar. The bar is Smarty, rendered by PHP as a sibling of the `#app` mount point, so no React-layer change can suppress it. Separating this from the menu migration matters because the two have different risk profiles and different reviewers: the migration is additive and reversible, while the header touches templates every team's pages render, and getting it wrong is visible to every merchant rather than only to partners.

### What?

On Partner Portal pages the top bar shows the Partner Portal logo and the user dropdown, and nothing else — search, Shoptet University, notifications, helpdesk, help, the design toggle and the markets switcher are all gone from that bar. Everywhere else in the admin the header is unchanged. The user dropdown keeps its current contents, because the design shows the same two lines it already renders: the user's name and `ID: <projectId>`. The recommended mechanism is a dedicated portal layout template rather than conditionals inside the shared ones — see Technical notes.

### Open questions

- Dedicated layout template or conditionals in the shared one? `cms2_admin_section_map.layoutTemplate` exists for exactly this and has four precedents in `admin/templates/layout/` (`empty.tpl`, `singleColumn.tpl`, `sofaEditor.tpl`, `themeEditor.tpl`). It leaves the shared header untouched, at the cost of a duplicated layout to keep in sync. Recommendation is the dedicated template; note it makes this subtask depend on the migration subtask, because `layoutTemplate` is set per section-map row.
- Should the superadmin item survive? It is invisible to partners and is how support reaches CRM and the project proxy; removing it makes the design literal but costs support a route. Recommendation is to keep it.
- Removing notifications means a partner working inside the portal never sees a system notification while on those pages. Confirm with Partnership that this is intended rather than an omission in the design.
- Does the portal need the footer from frame 739:11678 — „ID projektu / Server" plus the VOP and privacy links? It differs from the current admin footer and is not in this ticket's scope as written.
- The design shows the portal's own sidebar as the whole sidebar, with its four items at top level. In the real admin those items are children of the „Portál partnera" row, so the rest of the merchant's menu is still there beside them. Is the intent eventually a portal-only sidebar (which the dedicated layout template would make possible), or the portal branch inside the normal menu? This decides how much of the design is reachable at all.

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Opus 5, 2026-09-23_

- **The header is not React and cannot be overridden from React. **`admin/templates/layout/layout.tpl:10-38` builds the page grid: `:11-13` is `<header class="pageGrid__header">` including `afterHeader.tpl`, `:14-16` is the sidebar including `navigation.tpl`, and `:34-36` is `<div id="app">` — the only node React mounts into. Header and sidebar are siblings of it.
- `afterHeader.tpl` is four lines: the mobile menu toggle, `after_header/logo.tpl`, `after_header/searchForm.tpl` and `after_header/headerNavigation.tpl`. Two of those three includes disappear on portal pages, which is why a separate layout template is cleaner than conditionals.
- **Paths moved. **Commit `9947faafc58e` (CZ3FRA1-133) moved `admin/react/` to `frontend/apps/admin-web/`. On master the portal frontend is `frontend/apps/admin-web/src/PartnerPortal/` — three files, all under `pages/PartnerPortalOverview/`. Any older ticket text naming `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/` is stale, and the unmerged `CZ3TDR1-659` branch is still written against the old path.
- `PageLayoutDefault` takes no props at all: its props type is `React.ReactNode` and Inertia calls it as `layout(children)`, so there is no `hideHeader` or slot to pass. Opting out is all-or-nothing via `PageLayoutBlank`, as `SofaEditor` and `ThemeEditor` do.
- The portal overview page sets no `layout` property, so it picks up the default implicitly via `frontend/apps/admin-web/src/index.tsx:46`.
- The user item already renders both lines the design asks for — the user's full name and `ID: {$project->getId()}` — so no new data is needed, only the surrounding removals and the logo swap.
- **Ownership is split. **The Smarty chrome (`admin/templates/layout/layout.tpl`, `afterHeader.tpl`, `after_header/*`) matches no CODEOWNERS rule, so it has no mandatory reviewer despite being shared by every team. `frontend/apps/admin-web/src/PartnerPortal/**` is `@shoptet/devrel-team` (CODEOWNERS :584-588) while the layout components fall under the blanket `@shoptet/frontend-team` rule — a PR touching both needs two approvals. Ask Frontend for a review even where CODEOWNERS does not force one.
- No Cypress or PHPUnit coverage exists for the Partner Portal today, so the visual checks above are the only safety net.
